name: SIGTYP 2024 shared task on word embedding evaluation for 13 ancient and historical languages
description: This thesis focuses on the development, evaluation and application of computational methods tailored to ancient and historical languages, with a particular focus on Irish across its written history, from 7th-century Old Irish to pre-reform Modern Irish of the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Historical languages pose major challenges for NLP due to limited and noisy data, extensive orthographic and grammatical variation and diachronic change, which limit the applicability of tools designed for modern languages. The research investigates three key questions: how to evaluate word and subword embeddings for historical data, whether transfer learning across historical stages of a language is effective, and how such models can be applied in practice, using post-OCR correction for historical Irish as a case study. The methodology combines intrinsic evaluation, using analogy and similarity tasks, with extrinsic evaluation through downstream applications including part-of-speech tagging, morphological analysis, lemmatisation and masked language modelling. The thesis demonstrates that standard evaluation methods are often ill-suited to historical data and must be adapted to account for linguistic variation and annotation uncertainty. It introduces new datasets and benchmarks for embedding evaluation, including the organisation of the SIGTYP 2024 shared task on word embedding evaluation for 13 ancient and historical languages, the first benchmark of its kind.
